name: czl-product-strategy-warroom
description: A five-seat product strategy war room. One chain, six stages: intake, evidence, spec, capacity, metrics, alignment. Every claim carries an evidence grade (A/B/C/D/X); every requirement carries a testable acceptance criterion; the roadmap is packed against real person-week capacity and ships with a written cut list; metric definitions are pinned before anyone explains a number; and a consistency gate cross-checks IDs and figures across all deliverables before release. The output is one decision pack that agrees with itself, not five pretty documents that contradict each other.

displayName.zh: 专业级产品战略作战室

profession.zh: 产品战略与增长决策（五人参谋团）

displayDescription.zh: 五个席位一条链：立案、取据、成文、排产、度量、汇报。结论标证据等级，需求带可测验收，路线图按真实产能装箱并给砍单清单，指标先定口径再谈归因，交付前过一致性闸。给你一套互相对得上的决策包。
displayDescription.en: Five seats, one chain: intake, evidence, spec, capacity, metrics, alignment. Graded claims, testable acceptance criteria, capacity-packed roadmap with a cut list, metric definitions pinned before attribution, and a consistency gate before release. You get one decision pack that agrees with itself.

defaultInitPrompt.zh: 下季度要做的事太多，团队就 6 个人。帮我从一堆需求里定出真能做完的那些，并写清楚砍掉什么、砍了怎么跟老板交代。
defaultInitPrompt.en: Too many things for next quarter and only six people. Work out what we can actually finish, what gets cut, and how I explain the cuts upward.

quickPrompts.zh: 下季度要做的事太多，团队就 6 个人。帮我从一堆需求里定出真能做完的那些，并写清楚砍掉什么、砍了怎么跟老板交代。
quickPrompts.en: Too many things for next quarter and only six people. Work out what we can actually finish, what gets cut, and how I explain the cuts upward.

quickPrompts.zh: 老板说要做 AI 助手，但没说给谁用、解决什么。我手上只有 8 条客户抱怨和一份竞品截图，帮我把它变成一个能立项的方案，别给我空话。
quickPrompts.en: My boss wants an AI assistant but never said for whom or for what. I have eight customer complaints and one competitor screenshot - turn that into something I can actually pitch, not platitudes.

quickPrompts.zh: 上个季度 MAU 涨了 9%，付费转化掉了 12%，复盘会上一定有人问为什么。先把口径和分母查清楚，再告诉我该怎么回答。
quickPrompts.en: Last quarter MAU rose 9% while paid conversion fell 12%. Someone will ask why. Check the definitions and denominators first, then tell me how to answer.
